record.paper_title: Open problems concerning the Hőlder continuity of the direction of vorticity for the Navier-Stokes equations.
record.original_question: Let u be a Leray-Hopf weak solution of the three-dimensional evolution Navier-Stokes equations in R^3 on (0,T), with vorticity ω = ∇×u and vorticity-direction angle θ(x,y,t). If the direction of vorticity satisfies the β-Hölder condition sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x-y|^β for some β < 1/2, can one prove a finite-time vorticity integrability improvement, namely that ω belongs to L^2(0,T; L^r(R^3)) for some exponent r > 2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $u:\mathbb{R}^3\times(0,T)\to\mathbb{R}^3$ be a Leray–Hopf weak solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
$$\partial_t u+(u\cdot\nabla)u-\Delta u+\nabla p=0,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0,$$
with finite initial energy. Let $\omega=\nabla\times u$ denote the vorticity, and for points $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^3$ with $\omega(x,t)\neq 0$ and $\omega(y,t)\neq 0$, let $\theta(x,y,t)$ denote the angle between the unit vectors $\omega(x,t)/|\omega(x,t)|$ and $\omega(y,t)/|\omega(y,t)|$. Assume that there exist constants $c>0$ and $\beta\in(0,1/2)$ such that
$$|\sin\theta(x,y,t)|\le c\,|x-y|^{\beta}$$
for almost every $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^3$ and $t\in(0,T)$.

Prove or disprove: under these hypotheses, there exists an exponent $r>2$ such that
$$\omega\in L^{2}\bigl(0,T;\,L^{r}(\mathbb{R}^3)\bigr).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of a set of open problems on the role of Hölder continuity of the direction of the vorticity for the 3D Navier–Stokes equations. The borderline case β = 1/2 is known to yield ω ∈ L^∞(L^2) and regularity (Beirão da Veiga–Berselli, 2002), but the sub-critical case β < 1/2 — including the proposed L^2(0,T;L^r) integrability improvement for some r > 2 — remains an open problem according to subsequent surveys and follow-up papers, with no resolution found in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Navier-Stokes equations: Some questions related to the direction of the vorticity
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems linking β-Hölder continuity of vorticity direction to integrability improvements; β < 1/2 case remains unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: The β < 1/2 finite-time integrability improvement problem is reiterated as open in subsequent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Open problems concerning the Holder continuity of the direction of vorticity for the Navier-Stokes equations
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the integrability improvement ω ∈ L^2(0,T;L^r) with r > 2 under β < 1/2 as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as open.
